facts.value: Courses completed at a university are generally credited only if they were completed no more than five calendar years prior to starting the Master's program.
An application for credit transfer must be submitted with the application for admission.
A proof of all previously completed courses at a university (detailed performance record) must be submitted with the application for credit transfer.
Credits from a Bachelor's program cannot be transferred to the Master's program.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.
The ranking of applicants is based on a value that consists of 60% from the grade of the required degree and 40% from the grade of the study exposé.

The evaluation of the study exposé considers the external quality and representation, particularly the study motivation, professional perspective, and previously acquired knowledge in economic education and quantitative methods.
The application is done through an online system provided and operated by uni-assist e.V.
The online application allows for paperless application submissions and documents such as CV and certificates can be digitally uploaded and linked to the application.
Authenticated copies of required documents must be submitted upon enrollment in the new program.
Applicants with foreign degrees must demonstrate at least German language skills at the level of the Central Intermediate Examination (C1 level).
Every provisionally accepted applicant must take and pass the DSH-2 exam before the start of lectures.
If the bachelor's degree certificate is not yet available, applicants must submit additional documents by July 15.
A provisional admission can be granted under the condition of fulfilling additional requirements from the bachelor's program in economic education up to a maximum of 60 ECTS.
The semester fee for the Master's program amounts to approximately 350 € per semester.
Since the winter semester of 2008/09, no tuition fees are to be paid.
All completed examinations of the bachelor's program must be completed in the summer semester preceding the start of the master's program.
